thesis: This is an update to an existing short, not a new idea: the position was opened 2026-08-31 at 773 and is +1.1% with SPY at 764.29. An index that has barely flinched at a tightening Fed has not discounted one, and the October and December contracts price a hike-pause-hike path rather than a one-off.

thesis: UPDATE — close, thesis invalidated on discovery rather than on price. The insider tape is also a mild negative: one $1.74M sale and zero open-market buys in six months.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that MET is just a levered long on rates staying high, and I am buying it at the exact moment that view is most consensual — 81% priced, 3.76% off its 120-day high, after a 44% run off the low. thesis: UPDATE — exit, and stop waiting for a better price. The position is flat (entry 398.00, last 398.77), but the reason to hold it has failed an empirical test: inflation expectations repriced UP over this window — the Kalshi CPI >3.4% leg went 54c to 77c — and gold went DOWN, now 11.13% below its 120-day high of 448.70. Gold is not trading off inflation here, it is trading off the real yield, and a 4.95% 10y against ~3.5% CPI is a positive real yield that a hiking Fed widens further.
key_risk: Selling the classic inflation hedge in an inflation upturn is the uncomfortable side of this trade, and if Wednesday brings a hike paired with language that the Fed is behind the curve, gold can re-rate violently on exactly the debasement logic I am dismissing.
counter_argument: The strongest case for holding is that 3.5% CPI and a Fed forced into hiking is the textbook gold setup and the 520 target is a debasement call, not a chart level. Answered with the tape rather than by assertion: over the last six months GLD returned -14.59% while SPY returned +14.75%, a 29.34-point relative loss, through the very period in which inflation expectations rose. The hedge did not hedge.

thesis: NEW IDEA, and the only long initiated today. A life insurer earns the investment yield on its float, so it reinvests maturing bonds at whatever the curve offers — which makes a 4.95% 10y and a hiking Fed a direct earnings tailwind rather than the discount-rate headwind it is for almost everything else in this report. The tape confirms the mechanism is live: MET has beaten its own sector ETF XLF by 23.97 points over six months and 2.12 over three, and SPY by 26.46 over six, while the bond proxies that lose from the same move de-rate — XLU 11.14% off its high, GIS 15.05%, TLT sitting 0.25% off its 120-day low.
key_risk: The entire edge is the rate path, so a dovish surprise on Wednesday — a hold, or a hike paired with language that this is the last one — removes the reinvestment tailwind and takes MET back toward the 95.16 50-day SMA and through it. The insider tape is also a mild negative: one $1.74M sale and zero open-market buys in six months. Note also that the three-month edge over XLF is only 2.12 points, so most of the sector-relative outperformance was earned earlier in the year rather than recently.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that MET is just a levered long on rates staying high, bought at the moment that view is most consensual — 81% priced, 3.76% off its 120-day high, after a 44% run off the low. That is fair, and it is why size is 3% and the stop sits under the 50-day rather than under the last two days. What the objection does not explain is the 23.97-point six-month outperformance of XLF, which accumulated long before this week's repricing and is therefore not a bet on Wednesday alone.
